section_summary.extract_value: This section reports a path analysis (fully saturated, then trimmed) testing whether self-reassurance and body appreciation mediate relations between social safeness and eating/body-related psychopathology while controlling for BMI; the final model (Fig. 1) explained variance in self-reassurance (32%), body appreciation (56%), restraint (22%), eating concern (27%), weight concern (51%), and shape concern (47%) and showed excellent fit (χ2(7)=7.43, p=0.386; CFI=1.00; RMSEA=0.01). Direct and indirect effects are reported (e.g., BAS-2 correlated with BMI, and multiple significant indirect effects of social safeness via self-reassurance and body appreciation on eating/body psychopathology are described).
section_summary.evidence_source: Opening sentences: 'Path analysis was performed to explore whether the mechanisms of self-reassurance and body appreciation act as significant mediators...' and 'The recalculated model (Fig. 1) explained 32% of self-reassurance, 56% of body appreciation, 22% of restraint, 27% of eating concern, 51% of weight concern, and 47% of shape concern after controlling for BMI.'
